blocks.tr: Mimar Sinan, Osmanlı İmparatorluğu'nun en ünlü mimarı. Yaklaşık 1490'da Kayseri'nin yakınındaki Ağırnas köyünde, Hristiyan bir ailede doğdu. Ailesinin kökeni hakkında tarihçiler farklı şeyler söylüyor.
blocks.en: Mimar Sinan, Sinan the Architect, is the most famous architect of the Ottoman Empire. He was born around 1490 into a Christian family in Ağırnas, a village near Kayseri. Historians hold different views about the family's origins.

blocks.tr: 1512'de devşirmeyle İstanbul'a geldi. Devşirme, Osmanlı devletinin Hristiyan ailelerden genç erkek çocukları alıp devlet hizmeti için eğittiği bir sistemdi. Sinan burada Müslüman oldu, Türkçe öğrendi ve yeniçeri oldu. Birçok seferde savaştı: Belgrad, Rodos, Mohaç, Bağdat. Ordu için köprüler ve gemiler de yaptı. 1538'de Prut Nehri'nin üstüne on üç günde bir köprü kurdu.
blocks.en: In 1512 he came to Istanbul through the devşirme, the system by which the Ottoman state took boys from Christian families and trained them for its service. There he became a Muslim, learned Turkish and joined the Janissaries. He fought in many campaigns, from Belgrade and Rhodes to Mohács and Baghdad, and built bridges and ships for the army: in 1538 he put a bridge across the river Prut in thirteen days.

blocks.tr: 1530'ların sonunda sarayın baş mimarı oldu. Bu görevde yaklaşık elli yıl kaldı ve üç padişah için çalıştı: Kanuni Sultan Süleyman, II. Selim ve III. Murat. Bu dönemde yüzlerce yapı onun adıyla yapıldı: camiler, medreseler, hamamlar, köprüler, kervansaraylar, çeşmeler. Listelerde 350'den fazla eser var, ama Sinan hepsini kendi eliyle yapmadı. Büyük bir ekiple çalışıyordu.
blocks.en: At the end of the 1530s he became the chief architect of the court. He held the post for about fifty years and worked for three sultans: Süleyman the Magnificent, Selim II and Murad III. Hundreds of buildings went up under his name: mosques, schools, baths, bridges, caravanserais and fountains. The lists credit him with more than 350 works, though he didn't build them all with his own hands: he led a large team.

blocks.tr: Sinan'a göre ilk büyük eseri Şehzade Camii'ydi. Kanuni'nin oğlu Şehzade Mehmed 1543'te genç yaşta öldü ve padişah onun için bir cami istedi. Cami 1548'de tamamlandı. Sinan bu camiyi çıraklık eseri olarak görüyordu.
blocks.en: In Sinan's own view, his first great work was the Şehzade Mosque. Süleyman's son, Prince Mehmed, died young in 1543, and the sultan wanted a mosque in his memory. It was completed in 1548. Sinan saw it as his apprentice work.

blocks.tr: Süleymaniye Camii'nin yapımına 1550'de başlandı ve cami 1557'de tamamlandı. Cami, İstanbul'un yedi tepesinden birinin üstünde, Haliç'e bakan bir yerde bulunur. Çevresinde medreseler, bir hastane, bir aşevi ve bir hamam yapıldı. Bir caminin çevresindeki bu yapıların hepsine birlikte külliye denir. Sinan, Süleymaniye'yi kalfalık eseri olarak görüyordu. Kanuni Sultan Süleyman ve eşi Hürrem Sultan bugün caminin arkasındaki türbelerde yatıyor.
blocks.en: Work on the Süleymaniye began in 1550, and the mosque was completed in 1557. It stands on one of Istanbul's seven hills, looking out over the Golden Horn. Around it were built schools, a hospital, a public kitchen and a bath; a group of buildings like this around a mosque is called a külliye. Sinan saw the Süleymaniye as his journeyman work. Süleyman and his wife Hürrem Sultan lie in tombs behind the mosque.

blocks.tr: Sinan en büyük eserini seksen yaşını geçince yaptı: Edirne'deki Selimiye Camii. Cami II. Selim için 1569 ile 1575 arasında yapıldı. Kubbesi 31 metreden geniş ve dört ince, çok yüksek minaresi var. Sinan, Selimiye'yi en önemli eseri olarak görüyordu. UNESCO 2011'de Selimiye'yi ve külliyesini Dünya Mirası listesine aldı.
blocks.en: Sinan built his greatest work after he had turned eighty: the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne, built for Selim II between 1569 and 1575. Its dome is more than 31 metres across, and it has four slender, very tall minarets. Sinan himself considered it his most important work, and in 2011 UNESCO added the Selimiye and its complex to the World Heritage List.

blocks.tr: Sinan 1588'de, yaklaşık yüz yaşında, İstanbul'da öldü. Kendi türbesini de kendisi tasarladı: Süleymaniye'nin hemen yanında küçük bir türbe. Öğrencileri onun yolundan gitti; Sultanahmet Camii'nin mimarı Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa da onun öğrencilerinden biriydi. Bugün İstanbul'da gezerken bir kubbeye bakarsan, belki de Sinan'ın bir eserine bakıyorsun.
blocks.en: Sinan died in Istanbul in 1588, at about a hundred years old. He designed his own tomb too, a small one right next to the Süleymaniye. His students carried on his work: Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa, the architect of the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, was one of them. If you look up at a dome as you walk around Istanbul today, there's a good chance you're looking at one of Sinan's works.

journeyman, a craftsman between apprentice and master
complex of buildings around a mosque

questions.q: How did Sinan first come to Istanbul?
options: Through the devşirme, as a young man

questions.q: Which mosque did Sinan see as his apprentice work?
questions.explain: *Sinan bu camiyi çıraklık eseri olarak görüyordu.*

questions.q: Why does the text say *külliye denir*?
options: It is the impersonal passive: such a group of buildings is called a külliye
Sinan gave the buildings that name
questions.explain: *de-n-ir*, the passive of *demek*: **it is called**, by everyone.

sources.title: Sinan
sources.note: From Ağırnas near Kayseri, born before 1491; a devşirme of Selim I's reign; janissary on the Belgrade (1521) and Rhodes (1522) campaigns, then Mohács, Iraq, Corfu and Moldavia; a wooden bridge over the Prut in 13 days in 1538; appointed chief architect after the death of Acem Ali (1537); Şehzade (1548) his apprentice work, Süleymaniye (1557) his journeyman work, the Selimiye his greatest; a list of 452 works from period sources, about 350 in handbooks; died 1588 at about 100, tomb at a corner of the Süleymaniye complex

sources.title: Sinan
sources.note: Born c. 1490 in Ağırnaz; died 17 July 1588 in Constantinople; Süleymaniye Mosque 1550–1557; Selimiye Mosque, Edirne, 1569–1575

sources.title: Mimar Sinan
sources.note: Christian origin, Armenian, Greek and other views; conscripted through the devşirme in 1512; chief architect from 1539; at least 374 structures credited, 476 in the Tezkiretü'l Ebniye; Selimiye dome about 31 m; tomb of his own design just north of the Süleymaniye; Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa among his students

sources.title: Selimiye Mosque and its Social Complex
sources.note: Inscribed in 2011; built for Selim II; regarded by Sinan himself as his most important work; a single great dome of about 31.5 m

sources.title: Süleymaniye Mosque
sources.note: Founded in 1550 and inaugurated in 1557; on the Third Hill above the Golden Horn; madrasas, a hospital, a public kitchen and a bath in the complex; the tombs of Süleyman and Hürrem behind the mosque

sources.title: Şehzade Mosque
sources.note: Built by Süleyman for his son Şehzade Mehmed, who died in 1543; completed in 1548; Sinan called it his apprentice work
